name: Webflow forms
description: Webflow form submissions become Form Submitted events on the visitor's profile. A submission never subscribes anyone; a consent checkbox you map is recorded on the event, and only the fields you list are copied.

signature_secret.label: Webflow webhook secret
signature_secret.help: The secretKey Webflow returns when you create the webhook with a site token (or your OAuth app's client secret, for an app).

setup: Create the integration from this recipe and copy its webhook URL.

Webflow only signs webhooks created through its API. In Webflow, create a site token (Site settings → Apps & integrations → API access) with Forms read access, then: POST https://api.webflow.com/v2/sites/<site_id>/webhooks with {"triggerType": "form_submission", "url": "<webhook URL>"} and the header Authorization: Bearer <site token>.
Save the secretKey from Webflow's answer as the integration's signing secret.

In the integration's settings, set email_field to the name of the form's email field (if it isn't called Email), consent_field to the name of a marketing consent checkbox if the form has one, and copy_fields to the field names worth keeping on the event (for example ["Interest"]). Other fields aren't stored.
Submit the form on your published site and check the delivery log.

People this adds are held back from marketing. A form submission isn't an opt-in, so nobody is subscribed. To add people who ticked the consent box to your marketing, send them a confirmation (double opt-in) first.
